authorization_decision.required_successor: immutable superseding r5-or-later runner, seal, preflight proof, tests, and fresh independent QA

findings.title: Embedded authorization digest and raw-runner seal form a non-executable circular authority chain
evidence: scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v2.py:105 leaves AUTHORIZATION_SHA256 as a non-hex placeholder, and lines 1373-1380 reject execution until that literal is replaced by the actual authorization digest.
Replacing the single literal necessarily changes the raw runner bytes. The current raw runner is e210aac5de924e94de30a602158d074501a22de3d1301121d5eb74ad93c6a9b3, exactly the value pinned by r4 seal.
A read-only in-memory replacement with 64 lowercase hex characters produced a different raw runner digest (db9c7fc2c36b8b675ddea6ad00f71ce6b1e406b1f89b1347fd96e53672eec406).
Runner lines 1468-1482 require seal.runner_sha256 to equal the current raw runner digest, so the authorized runner cannot pass r4 seal verification.

The template additionally requires a new runner and seal after any sealed byte change while authorization itself pins the raw seal; embedding the authorization digest back into the runner closes an unsatisfiable runner -> seal -> authorization -> runner cycle.
findings.impact: No future PASS QA or correctly formed authorization file can make the sealed r4 package reach the numerical worker. This is a terminal executability defect, not merely the deliberate current not-authorized state.
required_fix: Keep the successor runner byte-immutable and remove the actual authorization digest literal as a code dependency.

Take the expected authorization digest only from an external capability such as P1_LONG_EVENT_SEGMENT_V2_AUTHORIZATION_SHA256, validate its 64-hex form, and held-read the authorization file against it.
Use the immutable raw or normalized runner digest as the seal trust root, then build the acyclic lineage runner -> seal -> independent QA -> authorization.
Create a new successor seal and rerun independent zero-fit QA; do not mutate or authorize r4.

findings.title: The sealed read-only preflight digest is guaranteed to change when authorization becomes real
evidence: Runner lines 942-945 include actual_authorization_exists, AUTHORIZATION_SHA256, and execute_authorized in the preflight object; lines 963-964 include that object in verification_sha256.
The sealed r4 verification digest 92178d551730af7f9910ef7d7a76f63ecef972ac06b83089411386d6597d5f6b was generated with (false, placeholder, false).
Any actual authorization necessarily changes those fields to (true, 64-hex digest, true).
execute_parent lines 2177-2183 require the post-authorization preflight verification digest to equal the pre-authorization digest pinned by r4 seal.
findings.impact: Even if P0-01 were patched in isolation, authorized execution would still fail before claim because the readiness digest transition is mathematically unavoidable.
required_fix: Exclude mutable authorization state from the immutable scientific/readiness verification payload.
Report authorization state in a separate authenticated receipt or normalize it to a stable sentinel in the sealed digest.
Add a zero-fit transition test that constructs a synthetic valid authorization and proves the sealed readiness digest remains identical before claim.

findings.title: Authorization authenticates held seal A, but parent and worker reopen an unbound seal B
evidence: Runner lines 1406-1419 held-read the authorization-pinned seal and return its value and digest receipt.
execute_parent lines 2172-2175 and worker lines 2013-2016 subsequently call _verify_seal, which reopens SEAL_PATH at lines 1468-1485 without an expected digest tied to held seal A.
The second seal supplies its own project_file_sha256 and other expectations, so a path swap can separate authorization/QA lineage from the seal used for execution checks.
findings.impact: A cross-seal path race can break the promised single transitive authority lineage before claim.
required_fix: Pass the held seal value and read receipt from preimport authorization through parent and worker without reopening the path, or require _verify_seal(expected_sha256=held_A_digest).
Add an adversarial A-to-B swap test that must fail before snapshot or claim.

findings.title: Worker snapshot inventory is self-declared and can execute an unpinned legacy runner
evidence: Runner lines 1597-1626 accept any nonempty manifest files map and verify each entry only against the digest declared by that same manifest; exact required path membership and runner-owned digests are not compared.

Worker state loading at lines 1982-1990 hard-pins only the legacy config before importing the snapshot legacy runner. The legacy runner itself is executed without a hardcoded digest check at that load boundary.

The execution module receives a hardcoded check later, but arbitrary legacy import code can already run before that check. A crafted hidden-worker manifest can therefore satisfy the self-declared inventory while substituting the executable legacy runner.
findings.impact: A purportedly authorized fixed screen is not cryptographically bound to the exact executable snapshot before claim; unregistered code could run in the worker process.
required_fix: Require exact equality between manifest inventory paths and a runner-owned expected inventory with runner-owned digests.
Load executable modules from held verified bytes, or at minimum verify path identity and digest immediately before and after module execution.
Add a direct hidden-worker adversarial test with a valid-shaped manifest and altered legacy runner that must fail before import and claim.

findings.title: Outer truth-derived interval audit runs before all outer predictions are frozen and journaled
evidence: Execution module _fit_outer calls _accepted_interval_audit for each fold at lines 1194-1199 before record_outer_freeze at line 1235.
_accepted_interval_audit lines 1072-1078 calls segment_training_targets with outer surface truth and anomaly_type.
The closure requires every outer seed prediction to be frozen and digest-journaled before any score or target-derived outer audit, and states that outer labels are evaluation-only.
findings.impact: The candidate is not changed by this audit, but outer evaluation truth is consumed before the mandatory all-fold freeze boundary, violating the one-shot label firewall and making the claimed chronology false.
required_fix: Before freeze, retain only target-free accepted interval geometry and prediction digests.
Move disconnected targets, disconnected precision, and every other truth-derived interval audit into _score_outer after record_outer_freeze.
Add a sentinel test that raises on any outer truth/anomaly_type access before the freeze journal event.

findings.title: Durable success can be misreported as failure if the worker exits after lock unlink but before stdout receipt
evidence: _final_success_commit lines 1939-1961 durably verifies and unlinks execution.lock, then _worker_execute returns and main prints worker_ok later.
Parent lines 2199-2205 require a stdout receipt before read-only verification.
The parent failure path at lines 2209-2232 records a failure only if the lock remains; with the lock absent it rethrows without recognizing the already complete 0999 terminal and manifest.
findings.impact: A narrow postcommit process failure leaves a valid durable success namespace but reports execution failure, with no safe automatic rerun allowed.
required_fix: When supervision fails and the lock is absent, perform a read-only completed-terminal/manifest/result verification and publish or return a deterministic recovered-success receipt.
Add a synthetic Windows test that terminates immediately after unlink and before stdout, and prove exactly-once success recovery without writes.
